industry: Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Loitering Munitions
thesis: AeroVironment is the U.S. leader in small unmanned aircraft systems (Puma, JUMP 20) and Switchblade loitering munitions, and the transformational $4B+ BlueHalo acquisition (closed May 2025) added space, counter-UAS, directed energy, and cyber to build a diversified next-generation defense technology company. FY2026 revenue jumped 141% to a record $1.98B with a $1.2B funded backlog and $2.7B of bookings, but heavy purchase-accounting amortization, a $241M goodwill impairment, and share dilution drove a GAAP net loss. With drone and loitering-munition demand accelerating globally, the thesis is compelling, but integration execution, negative free cash flow, and a premium valuation on adjusted earnings warrant a SPEC. BUY.

drivers: Global loitering-munition demand surges as Switchblade 300/600 becomes a standard tactical strike weapon for the U.S. Army and allied militaries
Puma, JUMP 20, and P550 small UAS win large multi-year procurement and foreign military sales programs
BlueHalo integration unlocks cross-selling across counter-UAS, directed energy, space, and cyber, lifting SCDE-segment margins
Capacity investments convert the $1.2B funded backlog and $2.7B bookings into rapid revenue growth toward and beyond $2.5B
Purchase-accounting amortization and one-time charges roll off, driving GAAP profitability and a re-rating toward peer multiples

base_case.assumptions: FY2027 revenue grows to $2.125B–$2.225B (per guidance) with adjusted EBITDA of $305M–$325M and non-GAAP EPS of $3.02–$3.34. BlueHalo integration proceeds on plan, funded backlog stays above $1B, and the drone and counter-UAS demand cycle remains strong, but heavy intangible amortization keeps GAAP earnings thin. The stock trades on an EV/EBITDA and forward adjusted-EPS multiple consistent with a high-growth defense-technology franchise.

risks: BlueHalo integration stumbles, synergies disappoint, or further goodwill impairments follow the $241M FY2026 charge
U.S. defense budget delays, continuing resolutions, or program reprioritization slow procurement of Switchblade and UAS
Persistent negative free cash flow and additional equity or convertible issuance dilute shareholders
Low-cost drone and loitering-munition competition compresses pricing and margins
Valuation compresses sharply as high-multiple growth names de-rate on any execution or funding disappointment

catalysts.event: Q1 FY2027 earnings — first full-year comparison lapping the BlueHalo close and margin trajectory
Switchblade and loitering-munition contract awards (U.S. Army LMAMS/Replicator and allied FMS)
BlueHalo integration and SCDE-segment margin progress; counter-UAS and directed-energy program updates
Revenue ramp toward $2.125B–$2.225B guidance and return to GAAP net income
Manufacturing-capacity expansion milestones for Switchblade and small UAS production

key_risks: Integration risk from the transformational BlueHalo acquisition, including large goodwill and intangible balances subject to impairment
Heavy dependence on U.S. government funding exposes revenue to budget cycles, continuing resolutions, and shifting priorities
Negative free cash flow and elevated debt and convertible notes after the acquisition and capacity buildout
Share dilution — diluted share count roughly doubled to fund the BlueHalo deal
Premium valuation on adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings leaves little room for execution missteps
Growing low-cost competition in drones and loitering munitions could pressure pricing and market share
